annotations.text:
The Programmer, with the grid as the page.

Six bands of chrome become two rows and a rail:
• Row A — the noun and the verbs. The source strip (Editing Q4 · 3 changes · Update · Revert) and Clear / Include / Record on one 40px row. The STAGE / LOAD / SAVE labels move into tooltips.
• Row B — what the grid shows. Output / Local / focused layer, the filter, Lit, Groups, Columns. Its explanatory sentences become tooltips; "Make layer" moves onto the Local values row in the rail.
• The templates ride the selection bar, one line, scrolling sideways — they only appear once there is something for a press to land on.
• The rail is 300px, drag-to-size, and collapses to a 40px strip. Under 1200px of content width it opens as an overlay over the grid instead of squeezing it.
• No outer padding; the sidebar defaults to its collapsed rail on the live views.
• Selection is neutral — a white edge on the row, a white marquee, a white tick — and colour is reserved for ownership, so a selected cell and a cell you own no longer look alike. The FX and layer marks share one right-hand gutter in every cell, so the value never runs under them.

Assumed: static mockups (not a prototype); the show is running with Q4 included; the ShowHeader and ShowBar are left as they are — the one-band option beside is separable.

Small viewports.

iPad: same two rows; the rail starts collapsed and opens over the grid. The 700–1000 show-bar arm is unchanged.

iPhone: the show bar becomes ONE row, 56px with its padding (DBO · BLIND · tempo · Q4→Q5 · BACK · GO) instead of chips plus a 52px GO line. Rows A and B go to icons; the templates scroll; the fixture column keeps its min(45vw, 260px) width and the value columns scroll sideways under a fade. The rail is a bottom sheet with a 44px handle naming the layers. The legend goes behind the key button.

iPhone landscape: below 500px of height the app header scrolls away with the page and rows A and B fold into one.

Two other places the stack could live. Both keep rows A and B exactly as on the Programmer page; only the rail moves. B is worth a second look if the width still feels short on a 24-column rig; C is the plan's own earlier sketch and is here for the record.
